ai_architecture.q1: Single call per feature (synthesis, destinations, itinerary, vote options, consensus). No multi-step reasoning or planning loop.
ai_architecture.q2: No tool use/function calling implemented. location_helper is a documented V3 stub, not built.
ai_architecture.q3: No multi-agent or sub-agent orchestration anywhere in the codebase or documents.
ai_architecture.q4: No retrieval/RAG. No vector store, no document corpus, no embeddings.
ai_architecture.q5: No long-running/async agent workflows. Every AI call is a single request/response inside an HTTP handler.
ai_architecture.q6: No cross-session memory. Only the computed result is persisted (aggregate_input_hash), not conversational state.
ai_architecture.q7: Yes — already solved with client.messages.parse(output_format=ConsensusReport) plus a code-level re-filter guardrail.
ai_architecture.q8: No LLM token streaming. SSE is used for app-state updates, not model output.
ai_architecture.q9: No prompt-management need. Prompts are short, inline, single-owner (services/ai.py), no non-engineer editors.
ai_architecture.q10: Yes, already built: backend/evals/ (harness, fakes, scenarios) wired into CI.
ai_architecture.q11: No dedicated LLM-call observability tool; folded into the general observability gap (r9), not AI-specific.
ai_architecture.q12: Yes, enforced in code: grounded-conflict filter against deterministic gap_flags, anonymity instruction backed by an eval assertion.
ai_architecture.q13: No multi-provider/fallback/routing. Anthropic only, not documented as a requirement.

recommendations.recommendation: next ^16.2.2 resolved to 16.3.5 (npm update, already inside the existing semver range)
recommendations.why: Installed 16.2.2 sits inside the vulnerable range for two critical unauthenticated RCEs (Windows path-traversal, AVIF image-optimization) plus nine high/moderate advisories (DoS, SSRF, XSS, cache-poisoning, middleware bypass). All are fixed by 16.2.5-16.3.3; the fix is a patch bump already permitted by package.json, not a migration.
recommendations.cost_impact: None — no infra or billing change.

evidence.note: npm audit on installed lockfile: 3 critical / 9 high / 6 moderate / 2 low total across the tree, next is the direct source of the two criticals

Both fixed at beta.32. This is a correctness/security defect in the exact library doing the Google OAuth -> backend JWT exchange the app depends on.

evidence.note: npm audit; critical severity, isDirect: true
